title: Rename the board's registered command from quest-board to quest
description:
Operator instruction, verbatim, relayed by opum-doc as seq 173 in opum-agent's OPAG-1089 dispatch, 2026-10-02: "change 'lore-pane' to just 'lore' and 'quest-board' to just 'quest'".

opum-doc's design: `/quest-board` becomes `/quest`, and the argument forms carry over -- `/quest full`, `/quest fleet|local|collapse|expand`, `/quest refs`. Pane ids, state keys and store keys stay UNCHANGED; only the registered command name and its `command.run` matcher change. This goes into 0.13.0. lore-cli makes the paired change to its own pane.

The opum-quest plugin also ships a SKILL named `quest`, so a command/skill clash is possible; opum-doc has ruled the name and choosing another is explicitly not this task's call, so the clash is checked in a live session and REPORTED to opum-agent with evidence if one exists.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The board registers no slash command -- neither `quest` nor `quest-board` is declared -- and `session.start` completes without the engine refusing a registration
The pane id, the atom keys and the store key are unchanged: quest-board remains the pane id and the ui.render requestId
Every doc, help string and release-note mention of the old command name is updated to the skill-routed form
The live-session clash check is reported to opum-agent with both commit SHAs

plan: 2. Rename the registered command and its command.run matcher to `quest`; leave the pane id, atom keys and store key alone
3. Update the hooks comment, the command description and the CHANGELOG release note
4. Check a live session for a command/skill clash against the plugin's own `quest` skill and report it with evidence
5. Run the mod suite and the repo gates; PR, green required checks, squash merge, prune
implementationNotes:
SUPERSEDED BY RULING, 2026-10-03 (opum-doc seq 176, relay ODOC-OP-2026-10-03-07, recorded on opum-agent OPAG-1089 at origin/dev 688d78ff).

The rename this task was filed for does NOT ship, because the live-session check it asked for CONFIRMED the clash and found it harder than lore-cli's case. Measured with `claude -p --plugin-dir <git archive> "<prompt>"`, cwd outside both trees, Claude Code 2.1.288:

| tree | prompt | reaches |
|---|---|---|
| pre-rename dc538b62 (origin/dev) | /quest-board | COMMAND -- "Quest board opened, showing the fleet." |
| pre-rename dc538b62 | /quest | SKILL (correct: the bare name was never the command's) |
| post-rename 037c155 | /quest | SKILL, and the mod fails to initialise |
| post-rename 037c155 | /quest full | SKILL, same failure |

On the renamed tree the engine REFUSES the registration outright and the whole session.start hook throws and is skipped:

  opum-quest: session.start hook rejected: threw opum-quest: $.command.register: "/quest" refused: it is the plugin's /opum-quest:quest

So the board would not initialise at all -- no pane open, no refresh clock -- not merely lose a name. `claude plugin validate --strict` and the mod suite both passed on the renamed tree (21/21); only a live session showed it.

opum-doc's decision, verbatim: "drop the `quest` command registration; the `quest` skill routes `dashboard`, `board`, `full`, `fleet` and `local` to `mcp__opum-quest__dashboard` (scope and full arguments); every other argument goes to the CLI." lore's parallel outcome was to drop the slash command and route through the skill.

READING APPLIED, stated so it can be corrected in one message: the `quest-board` registration goes too, not just `quest`. The operator's instruction was to change "quest-board" to just "quest", and the lore outcome opum-doc cites is "drop the slash command" -- so the end state is no board slash command at all, with the skill owning the name. The tool half lands with QCLI-441 in the same pull request, because dropping the command without it would leave the board unreachable.
